title: Unnecessary String Allocations for Enum Representation
pattern: Using raw heap-allocated strings (`String`) to represent state categories, flags, or finite enum tags instead of proper compiler-checked Rust `enum` types.
why_bad: Comparing and allocating strings requires costly heap allocations, memory hashing, and pointer dereferencing on every status change or lookup. Enums are represented as small integers (usually 1 byte) and compared in a single CPU cycle with full compiler safety [317, 350].
detection: Fields named `status`, `kind`, `category`, or `state` typed as `String`, where strings like `"success"`, `"error"`, `"active"` are passed or compared regularly.
counterexample: The statuses are dynamic, user-configured strings loaded from an external file at runtime that cannot be known at compile-time. `Context-dependent`.
source: *A Philosophy of Software Design*, Chapter 20 (p. 317); *Code Complete*, Section 25.3 (p. 350).
